description: Package declares the manufacturer's name and complete address; or, if the manufacturer is not the packer, the names and addresses of both manufacturer and packer; or, for imported packages, the importer's name and address.

exceptions.modified_requirement: An identifying mark or inscription sufficient for a consumer to identify the manufacturer/packer/importer satisfies this rule; a full address is not required.

review_note: Explanation III to this clause states that for food-article packages, 'the provisions of this sub-rule shall not apply' and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (now superseded by FSSAI's own regulations) applies instead. It is genuinely ambiguous whether 'this sub-rule' means clause (a) alone or all of sub-rule 6(1) -- Indian legislative drafting sometimes uses 'sub-rule' loosely. Rule 6(1)(d) carries its own separate, explicit food carve-out (see lmpc_6_1_d), which would be redundant if Explanation III already exempted the whole of 6(1) -- that's the basis for reading Explanation III as scoped to clause (a) only. This rule is currently kept active for packaged_food because FSSAI's own labelling regulations independently require the same address declaration, so the functional check is correct either way -- only the exact legal citation is uncertain. Confirm against the current consolidated LMPC text or FSSAI Packaging & Labelling Regulations before final submission, and update source_citation accordingly if it should cite FSSAI instead.
